title: 5 Practical Paths to Green Card Sponsorship for Nurses
summary: Explore five practical ways to find healthcare employers offering permanent jobs and Green Card sponsorship.
body_text: If you are a nurse looking for Green Card sponsorship in the United States, one of the hardest parts may be figuring out where to start. ‍ Should you ask your current hospital? Apply directly to employers? Work with a healthcare recruitment company? Move to another state? ‍ There is no single easy route, and no employer can guarantee that a Green Card will ultimately be approved. But there are practical ways to look for the right opportunity. ‍ For most nurses pursuing an employment-based Green Card, the starting point is not the Green Card application itself. It is finding a permanent nursing job with a healthcare employer that is willing to sponsor you. ‍ This guide focuses on five practical paths nurses can use to find that kind of opportunity. ‍ Can Nurses Get Green Card Sponsorship in the U.S.? ‍ Yes. Qualified nurses can pursue permanent residency through U.S. healthcare employers that are willing to offer qualifying permanent jobs and support an employment-based Green Card process. ‍ For many Registered Nurses (RNs), this is commonly associated with the EB-3 employment-based immigration category. ‍ RNs also have an important distinction under U.S. immigration rules. Professional nurses are included in a category known as Schedule A . This means the federal government has already identified professional nursing as an occupation with an insufficient supply of qualified U.S. workers. ‍ That can simplify one part of the employment-based process compared with many other occupations. ‍ It does not mean that every nurse automatically qualifies for a Green Card. The nurse still needs a qualifying employer, the appropriate credentials, and an immigration pathway that works for their individual situation. Visa availability can also affect when permanent residency can be completed. ‍ It is also important not to assume that every nursing role follows exactly the same process. Requirements for an RN, Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN), Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA), and other healthcare professionals can differ. ‍ The practical question for most nurses is therefore: ‍ How do I find an employer that is willing to hire me permanently and sponsor my Green Card? ‍ Here are five places to start. ‍ 1. Ask Whether Your Current Healthcare Employer Offers Green Card Sponsorship ‍ If you are already working for a hospital, nursing facility, health system, or another healthcare organization in the United States, you may not have to start your job search from scratch. ‍ Your current employer may already have a permanent residency sponsorship program. ‍ The problem is that many nurses never ask. ‍ Others ask a question that is too broad, such as: ‍ “Do you offer visa sponsorship?” ‍ That question can lead to an unclear answer because temporary visa sponsorship and Green Card sponsorship are not the same thing . ‍ Instead, ask specifically whether the organization offers employment-based permanent residency or Green Card sponsorship for nurses . ‍ Your manager may not know the answer. Human resources, talent acquisition, global mobility, or an immigration team may be better places to ask. ‍ 2. Apply Directly to Healthcare Employers That Offer Green Card Sponsorship If your current employer does not sponsor Green Cards, applying directly to healthcare organizations is another practical path. ‍ Potential employers may include: Hospitals Health systems Skilled nursing facilities Long-term care organizations Rehabilitation facilities Behavioral health facilities Other healthcare organizations with permanent nursing needs ‍ The important part is not simply finding a nursing job. ‍ It is determining whether the employer is actually prepared to support an employment-based Green Card process. ‍ Looking for a sponsoring healthcare employer? Let Flint help you find a nurse Green Card sponsorship opportunity Instead of searching for sponsoring employers one by one, you can apply through Flint. If you are already in the U.S., Flint can review your nursing experience, licensing, work authorization, and role fit against current healthcare facility opportunities that may include employer-sponsored Green Card pathways. ✓ Job-first placement process ✓ No fee to join Flint's candidate program ✓ Placement and sponsorship coordination Start Your Application Applying does not guarantee placement or Green Card sponsorship. Eligibility and available opportunities depend on your credentials, work authorization, employer requirements, current openings, and other individual circumstances. ‍ Search Specifically for Green Card Sponsorship ‍ A job advertisement that says “sponsorship available” may sound promising, but it does not always tell you what type of sponsorship is being offered. ‍ Look for language such as: Green Card sponsorship Permanent residency sponsorship Employment-based sponsorship EB-3 sponsorship Permanent nursing positions with sponsorship ‍ If the listing only says “visa sponsorship,” ask for clarification. ‍ You want to know whether the organization is discussing a temporary work visa, permanent residency, or both. ‍ Ask Who the Actual Sponsoring Employer Will Be ‍ This matters more than many candidates realize. ‍ If you find an opportunity through a recruiter, staffing organization, or third-party company, ask: ‍ Who will actually employ me? ‍ And then: ‍ Which organization will sponsor the Green Card process? ‍ Those answers should be clear. ‍ A recruitment company may help connect you with a position while the healthcare facility becomes your actual employer and sponsoring organization. ‍ Knowing the difference helps you understand who is making the job offer, who controls your employment, and who is responsible for the sponsorship process. ‍ Look Beyond the Word “Sponsorship” Before accepting a sponsored nursing position, ask about the actual terms. ‍ For example: Is the position permanent and full-time? Which facility will employ you? What nursing unit or specialty will you work in? Where is the job located? Is relocation required? Who pays the immigration-related legal costs? Is there a required employment commitment? Are there repayment provisions if you leave early? When is the employer expected to begin the sponsorship process? What happens if your current work authorization expires while your immigration case is still pending? A Green Card is important, but you are also accepting a job that could shape several years of your career. ‍ The employment terms deserve just as much attention as the word “sponsorship.” ‍ 3. Consider Sponsoring Employers Outside Your Current City or State ‍ Many nurses begin their search by asking: ‍ “Which hospitals sponsor Green Cards near me?” ‍ That is a reasonable place to start. ‍ It can also narrow your options quickly. ‍ Green Card sponsorship opportunities depend on actual healthcare employers, open positions, staffing needs, and the employer's willingness to sponsor. ‍ Those opportunities are not distributed evenly across every city or state. ‍ If you are willing to relocate, you can consider a much wider group of employers. ‍ Geographic Flexibility Can Expand Your Search ‍ Imagine two nurses with similar credentials. ‍ One is only willing to work within 20 miles of their current home. ‍ The other is willing to consider several states if the position, employer, and sponsorship terms make sense. ‍ The second nurse has a larger group of potential employers to evaluate. ‍ That does not mean relocation guarantees sponsorship. ‍ It means geographic flexibility can increase the number of sponsorship opportunities you are able to consider . ‍ There is an important difference. ‍ Check Nursing License Requirements Before You Relocate ‍ Being open to another state does not automatically mean you can begin working there immediately. ‍ Nursing licensure requirements still apply. ‍ Depending on your license, the state where you currently practice, and the state where the employer is located, you may need to obtain additional authorization or complete licensing requirements before beginning work. ‍ The employer or recruitment organization should be able to explain what credentials are required for the specific position. ‍ Do not move based only on a vague promise that a job or sponsorship opportunity may become available. ‍ You should understand the position, employer, location, licensing requirements, and sponsorship arrangement first. ‍ 4. Work With a Healthcare Recruitment Company That Connects Nurses With Sponsoring Employers ‍ Searching for sponsoring hospitals one by one is not the only option. ‍ Some healthcare recruitment and placement companies work specifically with employers that are willing to hire healthcare professionals who need employment-based Green Card sponsorship. ‍ For the right candidate, this model can make the search more organized. ‍ A recruitment company may help with: Reviewing your nursing credentials Determining whether your experience matches available positions Identifying healthcare employers with relevant openings Coordinating interviews Explaining relocation expectations Helping organize parts of the placement process Coordinating communication related to employer sponsorship ‍ There is one distinction you should understand before working with any recruitment company. ‍ The Recruitment Company Is Not Necessarily Your Green Card Sponsor ‍ When people search for “nursing agencies that sponsor Green Cards,” it is easy to assume that the agency itself will always be the sponsoring employer. ‍ That is not necessarily how the arrangement works. ‍ A company may help recruit and place you, while the hospital, nursing facility, or healthcare organization that hires you becomes your employer and sponsors the employment-based Green Card process. ‍ Ask about this directly. ‍ You should understand who your employer will be before accepting a position. ‍ How Flint's Model Works Flint helps qualified healthcare professionals who are already in the United States connect with healthcare facilities that may offer permanent, full-time jobs and employment-based Green Card sponsorship. ‍ The healthcare facility is generally the candidate's employer and sponsoring organization. ‍ Flint helps coordinate the process, including candidate screening, matching qualified healthcare workers with available facility opportunities, interview coordination, placement support, and aspects of the sponsorship process. ‍ Flint's candidate program is offered at no cost to candidates. Facility partners generally cover legal and immigration costs associated with employer sponsorship. ‍ However, applying to Flint does not guarantee that a matching position will be available, that a facility will make a job offer, or that an immigration case will ultimately be approved. ‍ Current opportunities depend on facility openings and the candidate's qualifications. ‍ See where your nursing background may fit Explore nursing roles that may offer employer Green Card sponsorship Flint works with healthcare facilities that may have permanent nursing positions with employer-sponsored Green Card pathways. If you are already in the U.S., you can apply to have your credentials and experience reviewed against current opportunities. Common sponsorship path Registered Nurse RN For qualified RNs already in the U.S. who are looking for permanent, full-time nursing positions that may include employer-sponsored Green Card opportunities. RN opportunities may involve an EB-3 employment-based pathway and, where applicable, the Schedule A process for professional nurses. Licensing, experience, work authorization, and employer requirements still apply. Check Your Fit Priority nursing role Licensed Practical Nurse LPN For licensed LPNs already in the U.S. who are open to permanent healthcare positions with facility employers that may offer Green Card sponsorship. Opportunities depend on current facility needs, licensing, experience, work authorization, location, and the requirements of the specific employer. Check Your Fit Patient care role Certified Nursing Assistant CNA For certified nursing assistants already in the U.S. who are seeking long-term healthcare employment with an employer that may consider Green Card sponsorship. CNA opportunities may be available based on certification, employer needs, work authorization, location, and current facility openings. Check Your Fit Applying does not guarantee a job, sponsorship, or immigration approval. Role availability and eligibility depend on current employer needs, credentials, licensing, work authorization, location, and individual immigration circumstances. ‍ 5. Target Sponsorship Opportunities That Actually Match Your Nursing Credentials Finding an employer that offers sponsorship is only part of the equation. ‍ The employer also needs to have a position for which you are qualified. ‍ This sounds obvious, but it is an important part of a successful sponsorship search. ‍ A hospital may sponsor nurses and still be unable to hire you for a position that requires credentials or clinical experience you do not have. ‍ For Registered Nurses, employers may look at factors such as: Whether you have passed the NCLEX-RN Your state nursing license Whether you can become licensed in the state of employment Your clinical experience Your nursing specialty How recently you have practiced The requirements of the specific facility Your current ability to work legally in the United States, where applicable ‍ Why NCLEX Matters for Registered Nurses ‍ For RNs, passing the NCLEX-RN is especially relevant. ‍ Under the Schedule A framework for professional nurses, an employer generally needs documentation showing that the nurse satisfies one of the qualifying credential pathways, which can include passing the NCLEX-RN, holding a qualifying CGFNS certificate, or having a full and unrestricted permanent nursing license in the state of intended employment. ‍ That does not mean passing NCLEX by itself gives someone a Green Card. ‍ It does not. ‍ Think of NCLEX as one important professional credential within a much larger employment and immigration process. ‍ You still need an employer, a qualifying job, the appropriate immigration process, and ultimately government approval. ‍ Do Not Apply to Every “Sponsorship” Job You Find ‍ A targeted search is usually more useful than sending applications to dozens of positions that do not match your background. ‍ If you have strong long-term care experience, for example, an employer hiring experienced ICU nurses may not be your best match simply because the posting mentions sponsorship. ‍ Look for the overlap between: ‍ Your credentials + your experience + the employer's opening + the employer's sponsorship program. ‍ That intersection is where a realistic opportunity exists. ‍ What All Five Paths Have in Common ‍ The five paths in this article look different, but they all lead back to the same basic requirements. ‍ A practical nurse Green Card sponsorship opportunity generally needs several pieces to line up: A real healthcare job A nurse who meets the position's requirements An employer willing to support an employment-based Green Card process The appropriate nursing credentials and licensing An immigration pathway that fits the candidate's individual circumstances Visa availability and successful completion of the required immigration process ‍ This is why searching for Green Card sponsorship is different from simply searching for any nursing job. ‍ The more useful question is often not: ‍ “How do I find a Green Card?” ‍ It is: ‍ “How do I find the right permanent nursing job with an employer prepared to sponsor me?” ‍ Once you frame the search that way, it becomes easier to evaluate opportunities realistically. ‍ How Flint Helps Nurses Looking for Green Card Sponsorship ‍ Flint's current program is designed primarily for qualified healthcare professionals who are already living in the United States. ‍ Rather than offering a Green Card independently of a job, Flint follows a job-first model. ‍ Qualified candidates may be matched with healthcare facilities that have appropriate permanent positions available. If the facility selects the candidate, the healthcare facility generally becomes the employer and supports the employment-based Green Card process. ‍ Flint helps coordinate the placement and sponsorship journey. ‍ Candidates generally need to meet the requirements of the healthcare role, have appropriate U.S. work authorization that can remain valid while the Green Card process is underway, and be open to opportunities based on participating facility openings. ‍ For Registered Nurses, that typically includes meeting applicable nursing licensing requirements and having passed the NCLEX-RN. ‍ Because available positions change, Flint cannot guarantee a job in a particular city or state. ‍ The program is offered to candidates at no cost, and facility partners generally cover legal and immigration expenses associated with employer sponsorship. ‍ You can start with your current employer, apply directly to healthcare organizations that sponsor, expand your geographic search, work with a healthcare recruitment company that connects nurses with sponsoring facilities, and focus on positions that genuinely match your credentials. ‍ Whichever path you choose, remember what sits at the center of the process: ‍ A real permanent nursing job with an employer that is prepared to support your Green Card sponsorship. ‍ The goal is not to find just any employer that uses the word “sponsorship.” ‍ It is to find the right employer, understand exactly what is being offered, and make sure the job, your nursing credentials, and your immigration circumstances fit together. ‍ Frequently Asked Questions Green Card Sponsorship for Nurses: FAQs Here are answers to common questions nurses have when looking for permanent healthcare jobs with employer-sponsored Green Card opportunities. Can a hospital sponsor a nurse for a Green Card? Yes. A qualifying U.S. hospital or healthcare employer may sponsor a nurse for an employment-based Green Card when the nurse, position, and employer meet the applicable requirements. Not every healthcare employer offers sponsorship, so it is important to confirm the employer's policy before accepting a position. Can Registered Nurses get EB-3 Green Card sponsorship? Yes. EB-3 is a common employment-based Green Card pathway for Registered Nurses. Professional nurses are also included in Schedule A, which changes part of the usual labor certification process. The nurse still needs a qualifying employer, appropriate credentials, visa availability, and successful completion of the immigration process. Do I need to pass the NCLEX for nurse Green Card sponsorship? For Registered Nurses applying through Flint, candidates generally need to have passed the NCLEX-RN and meet applicable state licensing requirements. Passing the NCLEX is an important credential, but it does not by itself guarantee a job, sponsorship, or Green Card approval. Can LPNs apply for Green Card sponsorship? Yes, some LPN opportunities may be available through employers that offer Green Card sponsorship. Eligibility depends on licensing, work authorization, employer needs, location, the available position, and the candidate's individual circumstances. LPN sponsorship should not automatically be treated the same as the Schedule A process for professional nurses. Can CNAs apply for Green Card sponsorship? CNA opportunities with employer sponsorship may be available depending on current facility openings. Candidates generally need the appropriate certification and must meet the employer's job requirements, work authorization requirements, and other eligibility criteria. Can my current healthcare employer sponsor my Green Card? Potentially. If you are already working for a hospital, health system, nursing facility, or another healthcare organization, ask whether the employer offers employment-based permanent residency sponsorship for your position. Green Card sponsorship policies can vary by employer and role. Do I need to be in the U.S. to apply through Flint? Flint's current program is designed primarily for qualified healthcare professionals who are already living in the United States. Candidates generally also need valid U.S. work authorization that can remain active while the Green Card process is underway. Does Flint sponsor the nurse's Green Card directly? Generally, no. Flint helps connect qualified candidates with healthcare facilities that may offer permanent jobs and employer-sponsored Green Card pathways. The healthcare facility is generally the candidate's employer and sponsoring organization, while Flint helps coordinate the placement and sponsorship process. Is nurse Green Card sponsorship free through Flint? There is no fee to join Flint's candidate program. Facility partners generally cover the legal and immigration costs associated with employer sponsorship. Candidates should still review the terms of any specific job offer or placement because other personal expenses may vary. Is EB-3 Green Card sponsorship guaranteed? No. A job offer, employer sponsorship, or approved immigration petition does not guarantee final permanent residency. The outcome depends on the immigration process, visa availability, government decisions, and the candidate's individual circumstances. What happens after I apply to Flint? Flint reviews your background, credentials, work authorization, and experience against current healthcare facility opportunities. If there may be a match, you may move forward to additional screening or an employer interview. A facility interview does not guarantee a job offer, and applying does not guarantee Green Card sponsorship or immigration approval. ‍ This article provides general educational information and is not legal advice. Immigration eligibility depends on individual circumstances, and immigration rules, visa availability, and government processing can change. For advice about your specific immigration situation, consult a qualified immigration attorney. ‍

title: Amazon in the community: Here’s what’s happening in Seattle, Bellevue, and the Puget Sound
summary: Learn how we invest in the community, help power the local economy, and support our employees in the Puget Sound region.
body_text: Recent Updates July 27, 2026 6:56 AM From AI arcades to robot demos: Inside Amazon's Kids Day From building AI-powered video games to cleaning up a miniature ocean, kids got hands-on with the technology shaping their future. Last week, more than 7,800 kids took over HQ1 in Seattle for the annual Bring Your Kids to Work Day, a two-day interactive experience designed to spark curiosity and creativity in the next generation of builders. What kids experienced at Amazon's Kids Day Across more than a dozen stations, kids explored everything from virtual reality training simulations to horticulture under a microscope. At the Agentic Arcade, built using AWS, kids answered questions that helped AI create a custom video game—then got to play it. At Badge in a Box, they designed their own AI-powered stickers. The donation is part of a new three-year commitment from Amazon to GSF to honor military veterans and first responders, and will help fund first responder grants for state-of-the-art equipment. This includes resources like a revolutionary PeerConnect app , which provides peer support, wellness tools, self-assessment, mental health programming, and resources to Seattle Fire team members. The Department will also be equipped with 900 pairs of cutting-edge extrication gloves, ensuring hand protection in various rescue scenarios. “We are grateful to have been selected for this grant from GSF and Amazon,” said Seattle Fire Chief Harold D. Scoggins. “With nearly every dollar of our department budget allocated, finding the money for new equipment and training can be challenging. title: eligibility requirements
body_text: Basic Eligibility Income Requirements You are categorically eligible if you: Receive public benefits (SNAP, unemployment insurance, etc.), OR Have household income below government thresholds based on your household size Income guidelines vary by location: NYC and California : MIT Living Wage guidelines ( NYC , California ) Massachusetts : USDA/SAIPE Median Household Income guidelines You'll need to provide documentation of income/benefits later in the enrollment process. Justice System Involvement You must have been directly involved with the justice system through at least one of: Previous incarceration Previous arrest(s) Current or past probation/parole Participation in a pretrial diversion program In some cases: having a close family member affected by incarceration Geographic Eligibility You must live in one of our service areas: Massachusetts (multiple locations) New York City (all 5 boroughs) Sacramento, California Other locations as our job training programs expand CDL License Requirements Legal Authorization Must have an active driver's license Must be a U.S. citizen or legal resident (as of September 29, 2025 , work authorization alone is not sufficient) Language Requirement Must speak English proficiently Medical Requirements You must be able to pass a DOT Medical Physical Examination. Certain health conditions may require medical clearance from your doctor, including: Epilepsy Recent heart attack, stroke, or heart surgery Very high blood pressure Sleep apnea (without proper treatment documentation) Vision or hearing loss that cannot be corrected Use of certain medications like: Anti-seizure medications Medical or recreational marijuana Opioid pain medications (including Suboxone, buprenorphine, methadone) ADHD medications (Adderall, Vyvanse, etc.) Benzodiazepines (Xanax, Valium, Ativan, Klonopin, etc.) If you take these medications, the DOT Medical Examiner may require a clearance letter from your doctor stating you're cleared to operate a commercial vehicle. Driving Record Requirements DUI/DWI Restrictions Cannot have more than 1 DUI/DWI/OUI in your lifetime Cannot have any DUI/DWI/OUI within the past 7 years Must not have failed a DOT-administered drug test in the past Traffic Violations & Accidents In the past 7 years, you cannot have: More than 1 accident Any serious driving violations (reckless driving, hit-and-run, evading/not stopping for police, driving with suspended license, etc.) License suspension due to points In the past 3 years, you cannot have: Any accidents where you were at fault What if my driving record doesn't meet these guidelines? If your driving record includes issues beyond what's listed above, your application will be placed on hold . This doesn't mean you're disqualified—it means we need you to secure a pre-hire offer letter from an employer in our network who is aware of your driving history and willing to hire you once you complete CDL training. This step protects your time and ensures you have a real pathway to employment after graduation. Criminal History Requirements Pending Cases No pending criminal cases (must be resolved before enrollment) Conviction Volume In the past 7 years, you cannot have: More than 2 felony convictions More than 4 misdemeanor convictions In the past 3 years, you cannot have: More than 2 violent felony convictions Disqualifying Convictions You cannot have convictions for: Vehicular homicide or murder Arson, terrorism, or treason Kidnapping or assault with intent to murder Felonies committed using a commercial motor vehicle Human trafficking, slavery, or sex offenses Drug trafficking (possession with intent to sell at scale) Leaving the scene of an accident Sex-related offenses Note: Some drug-related felonies may be acceptable (excluding trafficking). Sex offense convictions create significant employment barriers. What if my criminal history doesn't meet these guidelines? If your background includes convictions beyond the limits listed above—but not the disqualifying offenses—your application will be placed on hold . Being on hold isn't a rejection. It means you'll need to work with us to secure a pre-hire offer letter from a trucking employer who understands your background and is ready to hire you after you complete training. This process ensures that your time and effort in our program leads to real employment, not just a certificate. Additional Requirements Over-the-Road (OTR) Availability Must be willing and able to work Over-the-Road (OTR), which requires traveling across state lines for extended periods If you're currently on probation or parole, you'll need written confirmation from your supervision officer at the time of enrollment that you're authorized to cross state lines for employment purposes Drug Testing & Marijuana Use Must be clear of marijuana use for the past 3 months minimum If you've used marijuana within the past 6 months, you'll need to test negative on a drug screen before enrollment in trucking school You'll be subject to random DOT drug testing once you begin training at the yard. Failing a DOT-administered drug test will create a permanent barrier to CDL employment in the industry Financial Obligations Must be current on child support payments or on a payment plan (being behind can result in license suspension) Required Disclosures You'll need to provide information about: Employment status and work history Public assistance received in past 6 months Household size and number of dependents Transportation and housing situation Time served in correctional facilities (if applicable) If you have any questions about our CDL program or other vocational program offerings, please email support@emergecareer.com. Read about how our CDL program works here .

title: Payload vs Strapi: Which Open-Source Headless CMS Should You Choose in 2026?
summary: Payload vs Strapi compared on architecture, databases, APIs, and published pricing. Strapi Growth starts at $45/month; Payload publishes no pricing page. Verified Aug 13, 2026.
body_text: Payload and Strapi are the two open-source headless CMS projects most Node developers actually shortlist against each other. Both are MIT licensed. Both are TypeScript-first. Both let you self-host on your own infrastructure with no vendor sitting between your app and your database. They diverge on almost everything else: how they install, which databases they run on, how you query content, and how much of their commercial pricing they are willing to put on a public page. Last verified: August 13, 2026. Every figure and feature claim below was checked against live vendor sources on this date: Strapi CMS pricing , Strapi database docs , Payload homepage , Payload enterprise page , Payload database docs , Payload on GitHub , and Cosmic pricing . Note: payloadcms.com/pricing returned a 404 at the time of this check, so no Payload list pricing is quoted anywhere in this post. TL;DR Payload Strapi License MIT MIT (Community edition) Architecture Next.js native, installs into your existing /app folder Standalone Node.js application with its own admin panel Databases MongoDB, PostgreSQL, SQLite PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQLite MongoDB support Yes, via the Mongoose adapter No. Strapi's docs state it does not support MongoDB or any NoSQL database Content modeling Code-first TypeScript config Admin UI Content-Type Builder, written to code APIs REST, GraphQL, and a Local API you can call directly in Server Components REST and GraphQL Published paid pricing None public at time of check Growth $45/month, 3 seats included Hosting You host it, or one-click deploy to Vercel or Cloudflare You host it, or Strapi Cloud Ownership Part of Figma Strapi, independent GitHub stars 44.1k 72.9k The architectural fork This is the decision that drives everything else. Payload installs into your Next.js app. It is described by its own team as the first Next.js native CMS, and it drops directly into your existing /app folder. Your frontend and your backend live in one codebase, one deployment, one repo. The admin panel is React and renders as part of the same application. The repo currently sits at 44.1k stars with roughly 15,790 commits. The practical payoff is the Local API. Because Payload runs inside your app, you can query your content directly in React Server Components with no network hop at all: import { getPayload } from 'payload' import config from '@payload-config' const payload = await getPayload ( { config } ) const posts = await payload . find ( { collection : 'posts' , where : { status : { equals : 'published' } } , limit : 10 , } ) No REST call, no GraphQL query, no serialization round trip. For read-heavy Next.js sites that is genuinely fast and pleasant to work with. Strapi runs as its own application. It is a standalone Node.js server with its own admin panel, its own deployment, and its own lifecycle. Your frontend talks to it over HTTP like any other API: const res = await fetch ( 'https://your-strapi.example.com/api/posts?filters[status][$eq]=published' , { headers : { Authorization : ` Bearer ${ process . env . STRAPI_TOKEN } ` } } ) const { data } = await res . json ( ) That separation is a feature when you have more than one consumer. A Strapi instance can serve a Next.js marketing site, an iOS app, and a partner integration without any of them knowing about each other. Payload's Next.js coupling is a real constraint here: if your primary consumer is not a Next.js app, a large part of the value proposition does not apply to you. Database support, and the MongoDB question This is the sharpest technical difference, and it eliminates one of these tools outright for some teams. Payload ships three official adapters: MongoDB via Mongoose, PostgreSQL via Drizzle, and SQLite via Drizzle. Its docs note that all field types work across adapters with one exception, the Point Field, which is not supported on SQLite. Strapi supports PostgreSQL (14.0 minimum, 17.0 recommended), MySQL (8.0 minimum, 8.4 recommended), MariaDB (10.3 minimum, 11.4 recommended), and SQLite 3. Strapi's own database configuration documentation states plainly that Strapi does not support MongoDB, any other NoSQL database, or cloud-native databases such as Amazon Aurora and Google Cloud SQL. If your organization runs on MongoDB, that single line settles the evaluation. Strapi is out. Strapi's docs carry a second warning worth reading before you commit: Strapi applications are not designed to connect to a pre-existing database that was not created by a Strapi application. If you were hoping to point a CMS at a database you already own, plan accordingly. Content modeling Strapi gives you a Content-Type Builder in the admin UI. You click through creating collection types and fields, and Strapi writes the schema files into your project. Non-developers can shape content models without opening an editor, and the result is still version controlled. Payload is code-first. You define collections in TypeScript: import type { CollectionConfig } from 'payload' export const Posts : CollectionConfig = { slug : 'posts' , admin : { useAsTitle : 'title' } , fields : [ { name : 'title' , type : 'text' , required : true } , { name : 'status' , type : 'select' , options : [ 'draft' , 'published' ] } , { name : 'content' , type : 'richText' } , ] , } Types are generated automatically from that config, so your data is typed end to end. Every schema change is a code change, which means it goes through review and ships with your deploy. Teams that want content modeling to be a governed engineering activity prefer this. Teams that want a content architect to iterate without a pull request prefer Strapi's builder. Pricing transparency Here the two projects behave very differently, and it matters for procurement. Strapi publishes its numbers. As of the verification date: Community : free forever, MIT licensed, unlimited entries and API calls, REST and GraphQL, role-based access control, community support. Growth : $45/month including 3 seats, then $15/month per additional seat. Adds Strapi AI (1,000 credits per month, additional credits at $1.50 per 100), Live Preview, Releases, and Content History with 30 days of retention. SSO is an add-on on Growth at $150/month plus $50/month per seat. Enterprise : custom pricing. Adds Review Workflows, Audit Logs, a SOC 2 report, and Content History extended to 365 days. Strapi also offers Strapi Cloud as a separately priced hosted option. Check their pricing page for current Cloud tiers. Payload publishes nothing. At the time of this check, payloadcms.com/pricing returned a 404 and there was no pricing link in the site navigation. The enterprise page lists capabilities including SSO, Publishing Workflows, A/B Variant Testing, AI Auto-Embedding, and enterprise AI features, with Visual Editor and Multi-Player Editing marked as coming soon. The only route to a number is scheduling a demo. The open-source core is genuinely free and MIT licensed in both cases. The difference is what happens when you need SSO or audit logs. With Strapi you can price that today from a public page. With Payload you book a call. The Figma question Payload's homepage currently carries a banner announcing that Payload is now part of Figma, linking to Figma's announcement . Being acquired by a company of Figma's scale brings real resources to an open-source project. It also introduces a strategic question that any team standardizing on Payload should ask deliberately: the roadmap now serves Figma's product direction alongside the standalone CMS use case. The MIT license and the public repository are meaningful protection here. You can fork, and your data lives in your own database. This is not a reason to avoid Payload. It is a reason to have the conversation before you build your content platform on it, the same way you would for any dependency whose ownership just changed. When to choose each Choose Payload if: Your project is a Next.js application and will stay that way You want your CMS and frontend in one repo and one deploy You are on MongoDB You want code-first, fully typed content modeling under code review Querying content in Server Components with no network hop is worth real money to you Choose Strapi if: You need one content backend serving several frontends, apps, or partners Your frontend is not Next.js You want non-developers building content types in a UI You are on MySQL or MariaDB You want to see the price of SSO and workflows before you talk to sales Where a managed CMS fits instead Both of these options make you responsible for infrastructure. You provision the database, run migrations, patch the server, manage backups, monitor uptime, and scale under load. That work is real and it is recurring, and it is the reason many teams that start self-hosted eventually move. Cosmic is a managed, AI-powered headless CMS that removes that operational surface entirely. There is no database to run and no server to patch. You get a REST API and a TypeScript SDK: import { createBucketClient } from '@cosmicjs/sdk' ; const cosmic = createBucketClient ( { bucketSlug : 'your-bucket-slug' , readKey : 'your-read-key' , } ) ; const { objects : posts } = await cosmic . objects . find ( { type : 'posts' } ) . props ( [ 'title' , 'slug' , 'metadata' ] ) . depth ( 1 ) ; Cosmic's published pricing as of the verification date: Free at $0/month (1 Bucket, 2 team members, 1,000 Objects), Builder at $49/month (2 Buckets, 3 team members, 5,000 Objects), Team at $299/month (3 Buckets, 5 team members, 20,000 Objects), Business at $499/month (5 Buckets, 10 team members, 50,000 Objects), and custom Enterprise pricing. Additional users are $29/user/month. The honest tradeoff: you give up the ability to run the CMS on your own hardware. What you get back is the engineering time you were spending on database upgrades and CMS deploys. FINN, the car subscription company, put the benefit this way: "Cosmic is: us never having to ask a developer to change anything on the backend of our website." Maximilian Wuhr, Co-Founder at FINN Start free with Cosmic or talk to our CEO directly . Frequently asked questions Is Payload free? The open-source core is free and MIT licensed. Payload does not publish pricing for its enterprise tier; the enterprise page routes to a demo request. Is Strapi free? The Community edition is free forever and MIT licensed, with unlimited entries and API calls. Paid features start with Growth at $45/month including 3 seats. Can Strapi use MongoDB? No. Strapi's database documentation states it does not support MongoDB or any NoSQL database. Payload supports MongoDB through its Mongoose adapter. Can I use Payload without Next.js? Payload is built to run inside a Next.js /app folder, and that integration is the core of its design. If your stack is not Next.js, Strapi or a managed API-first CMS will fit more naturally. Does Cosmic support GraphQL? No. Cosmic provides a REST API and a JavaScript/TypeScript SDK. Both Payload and Strapi do offer GraphQL if that is a hard requirement for your team. Which one is better for a team of content editors? Strapi's admin panel and UI-based Content-Type Builder are more approachable for non-developers out of the box. Payload's admin is capable and extensible, but content modeling stays in code. The bottom line Payload is the stronger choice when you are building a Next.js application and want the CMS to disappear into it. Strapi is the stronger choice when the CMS needs to stand on its own and serve many consumers, and when you want to price the commercial tier without a sales call. Both hand you the operational burden of running the thing. If that burden is the part you want to skip, a managed CMS is worth pricing out before you commit to a self-hosted platform for the next three years. Create a free Cosmic account and model your first content type in a few minutes. No credit card required. title: Email Deliverability Services: A Complete Guide for 2026
summary: Learn how email deliverability services improve inbox placement and sender reputation. Compare top platforms to find the best fit.
body_text: Email deliverability services help senders improve inbox placement through authentication management, sender reputation building, warmup automation, inbox placement monitoring, and deliverability analytics. A recent Validity benchmark found that 84.8% of messages reached the inbox globally, while 6.1% landed in spam and 9.1% went missing , meaning roughly 1 in 6 emails failed to reach the inbox even before content, targeting, or reputation were considered ( Validity's 2025 benchmark report ). That gap explains why a simple warmup tool isn't always enough. Basic tools automate sending activity, while a full deliverability service connects engagement, authentication, provider-level monitoring, list hygiene, and expert diagnosis into one operating system for email. Why Email Deliverability Services Exist A campaign can report strong delivery while producing weak visibility because accepted messages may still miss the inbox. Inbox placement tracks what happens after a receiving provider accepts the message: it may reach the inbox, enter spam, or disappear into another filtering layer. That distinction matters because delivery reports alone cannot show whether recipients can see a campaign ( Mailjet's explanation of inbox placement ). The commercial impact is significant. Global inbox placement stands at 84.8% , while 6.1% of messages reach spam and 9.1% go missing, according to Validity's 2025 benchmark report . Senders therefore lose part of their audience before copy, segmentation, or conversion strategy can affect results. At scale, small changes influence large volumes across Gmail, Outlook, Microsoft 365, Yahoo, and other providers. What the category actually includes Email deliverability services include platforms, consultants, and software-and-expert teams that improve the conditions affecting inbox placement. Their work typically covers: Authentication management: SPF, DKIM, and DMARC setup, alignment checks, reporting, and policy enforcement. Reputation management: Monitoring sender behavior, complaints, bounces, and engagement signals. Warmup automation: Generating controlled interactions to establish or rebuild sending reputation. Inbox placement monitoring: Testing message placement across specific mailbox providers. Deliverability analytics: Connecting technical issues with campaign and sender-level outcomes. Expert guidance: Diagnosing problems that dashboards cannot explain. Authentication configured in DNS does not guarantee that a sender is enforcing it. A warmup tool may exchange messages or automate opens, yet leave a misaligned DMARC policy, provider-specific filtering, or uneven Gmail and Outlook performance undetected. A basic warmup tool can suit a lightly used mailbox with clean authentication and modest sending. A fuller service fits teams scaling outreach, managing several domains, sending marketing campaigns, serving multiple clients, or recovering from spam placement. The trade-off is straightforward: warmup automates one behavior, while broader services add monitoring, diagnosis, and provider-specific controls. Core Features of Email Deliverability Services A strong service doesn't treat warmup as the whole solution. It combines several controls because inbox providers evaluate technical identity, sending behavior, recipient response, and reputation together. Warmup automation Warmup should create realistic engagement signals, not just a rising send count. Useful activity can include opens, replies, conversation threads, spam removal, and marking messages as important. Provider-level controls matter because a sender may perform well with Gmail while struggling with Outlook or Microsoft 365. Warmup also needs restraint. Artificially increasing volume without monitoring complaints, bounces, or authentication can make a weak sending system appear active without making it trustworthy. Authentication management SPF identifies authorized sending servers. DKIM helps prove that a message wasn't altered in transit. DMARC applies a policy when SPF or DKIM checks fail and provides reporting visibility. Microsoft's authentication guidance explains these roles, while NIST notes that DMARC can pass when either SPF or DKIM succeeds and aligns with the visible From domain ( Microsoft's email authentication guidance ). The practical issue is coordination. A company may have several sending platforms, forms, CRMs, and outbound tools. Each source must preserve alignment, or legitimate messages can fail policy even when individual records exist. Testing, analytics, and list cleaning Inbox placement testing shows where accepted messages land. Analytics then connect those results with spam complaints, reputation indicators, bounces, and engagement. List cleaning removes risky or inactive recipients before they continue damaging sender signals. Teams that also manage customer communication may find operational guidance useful, including this resource on boosting business with CallZent email support . The same principle applies to deliverability: reliable processes matter more than isolated sending activity. Expert support A specialist can distinguish a content issue from an authentication issue, a provider-specific reputation problem, or a list-quality failure. That diagnosis prevents teams from repeatedly changing subject lines when the problem sits in DNS alignment or complaint handling. Practical rule: Warmup activity without authentication, monitoring, and list hygiene is incomplete deliverability work. The Authentication Enforcement Gap SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records establish identity, but inbox protection depends on how consistently those controls are enforced. Teams often leave DMARC in monitoring mode while sending platforms, domains, and provider rules change around it. DMARC adoption has grown faster than enforcement. Mailgun's 2025 State of Email Deliverability report found that 53.8% of senders used DMARC in 2024, up from 42.6% in 2023 , while only 25.5% of DMARC users planned to enforce a stricter policy that year. It also reported that only 13% of senders used inbox placement testing ( Mailgun's 2025 State of Email Deliverability report ). Why configured doesn't mean protected Authentication can fail operationally even when DNS records exist. Review these failure points: A third-party sender is missing from SPF authorization. DKIM signs with a domain that does not align with the visible From domain. A newly added platform sends mail outside the authentication plan. DMARC reports are not reviewed, leaving legitimate failures undiagnosed. A policy remains in observation mode instead of progressing toward Quarantine or Reject. The practical work is maintaining alignment across every sending source. A CRM, form, outbound tool, or marketing platform can introduce a failure after the original setup is complete. Teams also need a defined process for reviewing reports, approving new senders, and responding to unauthorized traffic. Provider rules are operational requirements Gmail may mark unauthenticated messages as spam or reject them with a 5.7.26 error . Since February 2024, senders delivering 5,000 or more messages per day to Gmail accounts must authenticate outgoing email, avoid unwanted or unsolicited messages, and provide a clear unsubscribe option, according to Gmail's sender guidelines . Relevant implementations also require SPF, DKIM, DMARC, one-click list-unsubscribe, and valid reverse and forward DNS under Google's bulk-sender requirements . A practical process for avoiding the spam folder therefore includes policy enforcement, alignment checks, report review, and provider-specific monitoring. Basic warmup tools can help establish sending history, while full-service platforms are better suited to managing multiple sources and ongoing enforcement. Deliverability Needs by Sender Type Sender type determines which reputation risks deserve attention first. Sales teams sending personalized outreach need controlled warmup, realistic engagement, and complaint protection. Marketing teams need testing, segmentation, and list hygiene. High-volume senders must meet stricter provider requirements while enforcing consistent controls across every sending source. Google and Yahoo guidance sets a spam complaint limit below 0.30% , while industry guidance identifies 0.10% as a safer operating target ( bulk-sender deliverability guidance ). Audience quality and unsubscribe handling therefore affect deliverability directly. They are operating controls, not secondary campaign details. Deliverability Requirements by Sender Type Sender Type Primary Challenge Critical Features Volume Considerations Sales outreach teams Building reputation without generating unwanted-mail complaints Provider-level warmup, realistic replies, bounce prevention, complaint monitoring Increase sending cautiously and separate domains or streams where appropriate Marketing teams Maintaining engagement across campaigns and segments Inbox placement testing, list cleaning, spam score monitoring, analytics Segment audiences and suppress risky or inactive recipients High-volume senders Meeting layered provider requirements at scale SPF, DKIM, DMARC enforcement, one-click unsubscribe, reporting, provider monitoring Apply the Gmail requirements discussed earlier to Gmail-bound volume Recruitment agencies Managing mixed recipient and provider environments B2B warmup, provider-specific testing, content controls, reputation monitoring Keep recruiter, client, and marketing streams distinguishable B2B companies Uneven performance across Gmail, Outlook, and Microsoft 365 Provider-level warmup, placement insights, authentication checks, expert review Avoid assuming one provider's results represent the whole audience Outlook and Office365 can behave differently from Gmail, particularly in mixed B2B environments. Benchmark coverage reports provider-level variation, including weaker performance for some Outlook, Hotmail, and Office365 segments ( B2B deliverability benchmark coverage ). A single warmup schedule cannot account for those differences. Sales outreach may need gradual volume control and reply monitoring, while marketing programs need stronger suppression and campaign-level testing. High-volume operations also need authentication enforcement and report review across each sending source, not merely a completed DNS setup. The right service should identify where reputation is weak, then let the sender adjust volume, engagement, and monitoring by provider. Basic warmup tools can support sending-history development. Full-service platforms are more suitable when several domains, providers, or sending systems require ongoing oversight. How to Evaluate Email Deliverability Services Start by asking whether the service explains and improves real inbox placement, not just how many emails it sends. A useful evaluation connects warmup activity with provider behavior, authentication status, reputation, and the reasons messages are filtered. Examine the network first. Aged, real inboxes can produce more meaningful engagement signals than newly created or obviously artificial accounts. The provider should explain how its network operates, which interactions it generates, and how senders can control the warmup profile. Six practical buying criteria Network quality: Look for aged real inboxes distributed across the providers that matter to the sender's audience. Signal realism: Check for replies, threads, opens, spam removal, and important marking, rather than automated opens alone. Provider control: Confirm that Gmail, Outlook, Microsoft 365, Yahoo, and other relevant destinations can be monitored or targeted separately. Authentication depth: The platform should identify SPF, DKIM, and DMARC problems, including alignment failures and policies that are configured but not enforced. Reporting clarity: Reports should distinguish delivery from inbox placement and show reputation, spam score, bounces, and provider-level outcomes. Human support: Specialists should help when the evidence points to a DNS, content, list, or provider-policy problem. Red flags worth rejecting Avoid services that guarantee inbox placement. Mailbox providers make independent filtering decisions, and sender behavior can change results after a warmup program begins. Other warning signs include: Private inbox access: IMAP access or permission to read a user's inbox creates unnecessary security concerns. No authentication tools: Warmup cannot correct broken alignment or unmanaged sending sources. No provider detail: A blended score can conceal weak Outlook or Gmail performance. Activity without diagnosis: More automated sending does not explain why messages are filtered. No expert access: Self-service dashboards leave complex enforcement and reputation problems unresolved. Authentication deserves particular scrutiny. A completed DNS setup does not prove that every sending source is aligned, authorized, and subject to the intended DMARC policy. Check whether the service can expose those gaps and help teams enforce the policy across transactional, marketing, and sales systems. Teams comparing low-cost options can review Mailwarm's free email deliverability tools before deciding whether a broader platform is justified. Premium pricing makes sense when it covers real engagement, monitoring, authentication support, reputation protection, and specialist access, rather than send automation alone. A lower subscription price is not a saving if the service cannot show where messages land or why providers distrust them. How Mailwarm Approaches Deliverability Mailwarm was built for teams that treat inbox placement as a system, not a checkbox. Its product positioning combines warmup with monitoring, authentication support, provider-level controls, and access to deliverability specialists. That broader scope explains why it is evaluated differently from a basic warmup utility. The implementation choice that matters most is separation by provider. Gmail, Outlook, Microsoft 365, Yahoo, and SMTP environments can produce different results for the same sender. Mailwarm lets teams examine and direct activity by provider, so a weak Outlook result does not disappear inside one blended score. Security also affects the buying decision. Mailwarm operates without requiring IMAP access or permission to read a private inbox, reducing the mailbox data a team must grant to a third-party service. That can matter for companies with stricter security reviews or multiple client accounts. The platform's differentiation is the operating layer around warmup: Spam score monitoring Inbox placement insights Authentication fix tools Bounce prevention Custom email content warmup B2B and B2C warmup Deliverability analytics Each plan includes expert deliverability calls. Specialists can review SPF, DKIM, DMARC, DNS configuration, content, volume, bounce patterns, sender reputation, and provider-specific filtering. That support is useful when authentication is configured but not enforced consistently across marketing, transactional, and sales systems. Teams assessing the trade-off can review the Mailwarm features page . A basic tool may suit a single mailbox and a narrow warmup objective. Mailwarm's broader cost is easier to justify when the team needs provider-level diagnosis, enforcement help, ongoing monitoring, and specialist review rather than activity generation alone. Frequently Asked Questions About Email Deliverability Services What is email warmup? Email warmup is a controlled process for building or rebuilding sender reputation through gradual sending and positive engagement. A serious warmup system uses interactions such as opens, replies, threads, spam removal, and important marking rather than relying only on message volume. How long does email warmup take? The appropriate timeline depends on mailbox history, authentication, list quality, sending volume, and current reputation. A new or damaged sender should increase activity carefully and monitor provider-level placement instead of following a rigid schedule. Does email warmup improve inbox placement? Warmup can support sender reputation by generating positive engagement signals, but it doesn't guarantee inbox placement. Authentication alignment, complaint rates, bounce prevention, content, audience quality, and provider-specific behavior also influence results. Is email warmup enough to fix deliverability? No. Warmup won't resolve a misaligned SPF or DKIM setup, weak DMARC enforcement, poor list hygiene, excessive complaints, or provider-specific filtering by itself. Those issues require authentication checks, monitoring, testing, and operational changes. Why do emails go to spam? Messages can go to spam because of weak sender reputation, unwanted engagement, authentication failures, alignment problems, bounces, complaints, or content and audience signals. A delivery report alone can't identify the cause because accepted mail may still land outside the inbox. How does Mailwarm help improve sender reputation? Mailwarm helps senders build reputation, monitor inbox placement, and improve deliverability through real inbox engagement, advanced warmup controls, and expert guidance. Its platform includes provider-level warmup, spam score monitoring, authentication fix tools, bounce prevention, inbox placement insights, and deliverability analytics. Why is Mailwarm more expensive than basic warmup tools? Mailwarm costs more because it combines real inbox engagement, up to 100% replies to warmup emails depending on the plan, spam score monitoring, provider-level warmup, authentication tools, no IMAP access required, and expert deliverability calls included in every plan. Does Mailwarm need access to a private inbox? No. Mailwarm doesn't require IMAP access or permission to read a user's private inbox. That gives teams a less intrusive way to use warmup and deliverability monitoring. Your Next Steps for Better Inbox Placement Deliverability is a system, not a single feature. Authentication, enforcement, reputation, engagement, list quality, provider-specific testing, and ongoing monitoring must work together. A practical decision path looks like this: Light sending: A sender using a modest volume with clean authentication may only need a simple warmup tool. Growing outreach: Sales teams, agencies, and recruiters need real engagement, bounce prevention, and provider-level warmup. Campaign operations: Marketing teams need placement testing, list cleaning, complaint monitoring, and analytics. High-volume sending: Teams delivering 5,000 or more messages per day to Gmail accounts need layered authentication, unsubscribe controls, and careful provider compliance ( Gmail bulk-sender requirements ). Audit the current authentication setup, check inbox placement across the providers that matter, and determine whether the existing approach addresses the full deliverability stack. If it only automates warmup activity, the sender likely needs broader controls. title: Duos Technologies Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results
body_text: Duos Technologies Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results August 17, 2026 4:00pm EDT Download as PDF Related Documents NT 10-Q Filing PDF HTML Conference Call Replay MP3 Q2 2026 Revenue Increases Nearly 30%, Driven by Initial Ramp in AI and Data Center Deployments Over $100 Million in Growth Capital Secured Through Multiple Transactions Company Reaffirms 2026 Guidance for 25 MW Deployed and Over $50 Million in Revenue JACKSONVILLE, Fla., Aug. 17, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Duos Technologies Group, Inc. (“Duos” or the “Company”) ( Nasdaq: DUOT ), a leading provider of adaptive, modular, and scalable Edge Data Center solutions, reported financial results for the second quarter (“Q2 2026”) ended June 30, 2026. Second Quarter 2026 and Recent Operational Highlights Signed five-year, 55 MW hosting agreements with Axe Compute valued at more than $500 million, representing a significant commercial milestone in the Company’s strategy to develop and operate high-density AI infrastructure Entered into an exclusive term sheet with 0Lat LLC for a proposed structured lease across a 15-site, 225-cabinet Edge Data Center portfolio in Texas and Georgia, initiating a 90-day exclusivity and confirmatory diligence period Completed the sale of the Company’s wholly owned rail technology subsidiary, Duos Technologies, Inc. The divestiture marks the completion of a broader strategic repositioning and enables the Company to fully concentrate its resources on its Edge Data Center and AI infrastructure businesses through Duos Edge AI, Inc. and Duos Technology Solutions, Inc. Secured $111 million in contracted revenue with an investment-grade hyperscaler to provide 10 MW of critical IT-load capacity for five years at its Columbus, Georgia data center campus The Company now has 25 MW contracted with all 25 MW planned for deployment in 2026, demonstrating accelerating demand and an ability to rapidly design, manufacture, and deploy modular infrastructure in underserved Tier 3 and Tier 4 markets Received $50.4 million in proceeds from the sale of substantially all the assets of New APR Energy, LLC, in which the Company held a 5% minority stake of the parent company Closed $55 million registered direct offering with a single large institutional investor, providing additional financial support for the Company’s growth plans, including the acquisition of its Columbus facility and related infrastructure investments to fulfill contracted customer deployments and expand the campus Hosted six (6) open houses with additional events and grand openings planned, showcasing the continued expansion of the Company’s EDC pipeline to support increasing demand for AI inference, training, and high-performance computing workloads Added to the Russell 2000® Index as part of the 2026 Russell indexes annual reconstitution Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results It should be noted that the following Financial Results represent the consolidation of the Company with its subsidiaries Duos Edge AI, Inc., Duos Technology Solutions, Inc. and Duos Energy Corporation (“Duos Energy”). Total revenues for Q2 2026 increased 30% to $6.18 million compared to $4.77 million in the second quarter of 2025 (“Q2 2025”). Total revenue for Q2 2026 represents an aggregate of approximately $3.23 million of Technology Solutions revenue, $2.91 million of Services and Consulting revenue, and approximately $.03 million of Hosting revenue. The increase in revenue was driven primarily by the increase in Technology Solutions revenue, which was partially offset by a decrease in Services and Consulting revenue in connection with the Company’s continued reduction in the scope of services provided under the Duos Energy Asset Management Agreement (the “AMA”) and the sale by New APR of substantially all of its assets in May 2026. The Technology Solutions business unit provides manufacturer-agnostic infrastructure sourcing, integration, and value-added supply chain services supporting data center, AI, and enterprise deployments. The Company expects services revenue from both its hosting and technology solutions to increase throughout 2026. This growth is expected to be driven by the deployment of additional edge data centers coming online as well as expanding Technology Solutions revenue tied to growth in the data center market. Cost of revenues for Q2 2026 decreased 9% to $2.73 million compared to $2.99 million for Q2 2025. The decrease was primarily due to reduced costs associated with the previously mentioned AMA and the wind-down of AMA-related activities. Gross margin for Q2 2026 increased 94% to $3.45 million compared to $1.78 million for Q2 2025. Gross margin improved primarily due to the significantly reduced cost of revenues associated with the AMA and the growing contribution of the Technology Solutions business. Operating expenses for Q2 2026 increased 2% to $3.40 million compared to $3.32 million for Q2 2025. The increase in expenses was attributable to increases in sales and marketing expenses as additional resources were deployed to support business development for the Edge Data Center and Technology Solutions businesses as well as general and administration expenses. Net operating income for Q2 2026 totaled $0.05 million compared to net operating loss of $1.54 million for Q2 2025, our first positive operating quarter as a data center infrastructure company. The decrease in the loss was primarily driven by the favorable impact of increased Technology Solutions revenue, accelerated recognition of the remaining AMA-related deferred revenue, and improved gross margins. Net income before taxes for Q2 2026 totaled $53.64 million compared to net loss of $1.62 million for Q2 2025. The increase in net income was primarily attributable to the gain on sale of investments previously noted in connection with the sale of substantially all of New APR’s assets. Basic and diluted net income per common share was $1.61 and a loss of $0.14 and $1.37 and a loss of $0.14 for the three months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. Cash and cash equivalents at June 30, 2026 totaled $112.31 million compared to $15.47 million at December 31, 2025. In addition, the Company had over $15.90 million in receivables and contract assets for a total of approximately $128.21 million in cash and expected short-term liquidity. Six Month 2026 Financial Results Total revenues decreased 4% to $8.32 million from $8.68 million in the same period last year. Total revenue for the first six months of 2026 represents an aggregate of approximately $3.79 million of Technology Solutions revenue, $4.46 million of Services and Consulting revenue, and approximately $.06 million of Hosting revenue. The decrease in total revenues was primarily driven by the previously noted decrease in Services and Consulting revenue in connection with the Company’s continued reduction in the scope of services provided under the AMA and the sale by New APR of substantially all of its assets in May 2026. Cost of revenues decreased 32% to $3.82 million from $5.65 million in the same period last year. The decrease in cost of revenues was primarily due to reduced costs associated with the previously mentioned AMA and the wind-down of AMA-related activities. Gross margin increased 48% to $4.50 million from $3.03 million in the same period last year. Gross margin improved primarily due to the significantly reduced cost of revenues associated with the AMA and the growing contribution of the Technology Solutions business. Operating expenses increased 49% to $7.63 million from $5.11 million in the same period last year. The increase in expenses was largely attributable to increases in sales and marketing expenses as additional resources were deployed to support business development for the Edge Data Center and Technology Solutions businesses as well as general and administration expenses. Net operating loss totaled $3.13 million compared to net operating loss of $2.07 million in the same period last year. The increase in loss from operations was primarily driven by higher operating expenses, offset by growth in Technology Solutions revenue and accelerated recognition of the remaining AMA-related deferred revenue. Net income before taxes totaled $50.60 million compared to net loss of $2.44 million in the same period last year. The increase in net income was primarily attributable to the gain on sale of investments previously noted in connection with the sale of substantially all of New APR’s assets. Basic and diluted net income per common share was $1.70 and a loss of $0.21 and $1.41 and a loss of $0.21 for the six months ended June 30, 2026 and 2025, respectively. Financial Outlook At the end of the second quarter, the Company’s bookings represented approximately $43.5 million in revenue, of which all is expected to be recognized during the year, including contracted backlog and near-term anticipated awards. In addition, approximately $1.1 million of contracted Technology Solutions deferred revenue recorded in 2025 will be recorded as revenue in 2026, further supporting near-term performance. Duos Technology Solutions continues to add new customers and has approximately $28 million in backlog so far in 2026. Based on these committed contracts and near-term pending orders that are already performing or scheduled to be executed throughout the course of 2026, the Company is reconfirming its expectation for total revenue in 2026 to exceed $50 million. A significant portion of this revenue is anticipated to be recognized in the second half of the year, aligned with project timing and infrastructure deployments, supporting continued operating leverage and progression toward the Company growth strategy. Adjusted EBITDA for the second quarter of 2026 was $0.5 million. The Company did not report adjusted EBITDA in the prior-year period. Adjusted EBITDA was positive for the quarter, and the Company expects profitability to continue to improve as revenue ramps over the coming quarters and anticipates achieving positive adjusted EBITDA for the full year 2026. Management Commentary “In the second quarter and over the last several weeks, we have made tremendous progress both in operational execution and the fundamental repositioning of our business as a standalone AI infrastructure provider,” said Duos CEO Doug Recker. “Financially, we began to see the early stages of the substantial performance ramp we expect to build over the course of this year, highlighted by a 30% increase in revenue and a material improvement in profitability. We also secured over $100 million in growth capital through two major transactions: a $55 million direct investment with a single institutional investor and an additional $50.4 million in proceeds resulting from New APR's sale of substantially all its assets. “Operationally, we recently announced the successful divestiture of our legacy rail operations, which will now enable us to fully concentrate our resources on the Edge Data Center and AI infrastructure businesses. We also agreed to terms on a new $111 million, 10 MW contract with an investment-grade hyperscaler to provide critical IT-load capacity, adding to our already-substantial backlog and supporting our reaffirmed outlook to provide 25 MW of compute and generate north of $50 million in revenue by the end of this year.” Conference Call The Company’s management will host a conference call on Monday, August 17, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. Eastern Time to discuss these results, followed by a question-and-answer period.
